title: The Immense Value of North America
gist: Americas Society/COA chief Susan Segal argues NAFTA/USMCA integration is the world's most successful trade pact and that unwinding it would raise consumer prices, hurt SME supply chains and open North America to rival powers. She praises Sheinbaum's patience in defending integration.

themes.theme: History of US backstops for Mexico

insights.claim: The US government, via the New York Fed and Treasury, moved to support Mexico and contain banking-system damage after Mexico's August 1982 debt default, beginning a decades-long effort to integrate Mexico with the US.
insights.speaker: SUSAN SEGAL
insights.so_what: Precedent: Washington has repeatedly acted as crisis backstop for Mexico, relevant to tail-risk pricing of Mexican assets.

insights.claim: After the December 1994 Tequila Crisis and peso devaluation, US leadership prompted the IMF and other lenders to assemble a $50 billion package for Mexico.
insights.speaker: SUSAN SEGAL
insights.so_what: Shows the historical size of the official-sector response to a Mexican confidence shock.

insights.claim: NAFTA/USMCA was a deliberate political calculation that integrated supply chains and created thousands of jobs in all three countries, pairing Mexico's demographics with US and Canadian innovation, and the author calls it the most successful trade agreement in the world.
insights.speaker: SUSAN SEGAL
insights.so_what: Frames the defender's case ahead of USMCA review; useful for assessing political support for the pact.
insights.quote: It was by far the most successful trade agreement in the world.
insights.locator: NAFTA (more recently USMCA) was a deliberate political calculation

insights.claim: Separating from USMCA would make goods more expensive for North American consumers, especially in the US, and jeopardize the finances of many companies, particularly SMEs at the heart of the supply chain.
insights.speaker: SUSAN SEGAL
insights.so_what: Break-up risk is a cost-push and SME credit risk in cross-border supply chains.

insights.claim: Dismantling the old NAFTA essence would give other countries a path to take a leading role in North America.
insights.speaker: SUSAN SEGAL
insights.so_what: Geopolitical angle: US retreat from integration could cede Mexican and Canadian ground to rival powers such as China.

insights.claim: Mexico became the largest US trading partner as a result of NAFTA-era integration and investment across North America.
insights.speaker: SUSAN SEGAL
insights.so_what: Underscores how embedded Mexico is in US trade exposure.

insights.claim: The author praises President Claudia Sheinbaum for patience and a continued vision of an integrated, strong North America.
insights.speaker: SUSAN SEGAL
insights.so_what: Signals that business-establishment voices back Sheinbaum's non-confrontational line.
insights.quote: I laud President Claudia Sheinbaum for her patience and her continued vision for an integrated and strong North America.
